I want to buy a cheap, small pocket-sized computer like Raspberry Pi, Intel Edison, Beaglebone Black...does anyone have any experience/recommendations?

Lots of options and it depends on what you want to do. I've used raspberry pi and arduino personally. The arduino is really well supported, documented and there are a lots of upgrades you can do (shields) that make it easy to plug and play. The community out there is also very helpful and I've never had a problem getting help when I need it. There are also a lot of different boards already designed for different applications, I recommend starting with the uno but take a look at what's out there first.

Raspberry pi I haven't used nearly as much but it is similar in support to arduino and it has more power. You can find a lot of how to's and starter code for this one and it can virtually run as it's own computer.

What do you have in mind to build?

I'm just a coder wanting to learn more about hardware using some kind of cool embedded applications project...maybe some kind of real-time updating server video-streaming with a camera, or a generative music device that uses temperature/motion to generate music. Just starting out, so somethign simpler and easy to use would be great!

You can't go wrong with either really. Arduino may be a bit cheaper and most of the hardware is open source so you can look at the schematics. Most of my projects now I strip down the arduino to just an atmega and use as few components as possible, I'm sure that could be done with the raspberry pi as well. If you're goal is to learn more about hardware I would go for the arduino but don't take my word as gospel!
Arduino is more of an electronics prototyping platform. I think RaspberryPI would be better suited for your needs as it can host a full OS.
